ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher and send the driver's account to Ryde for review of the false "I'm Here" arrival confirmation + flag_account
ruling.reasoning: The driver, not the rider, cancelled the trip, so the cancellation fee can only stand through NS-0's driver-cancellation branch (NS-1/NS-2) [F3][NS-0]. The driver claims the rider never showed up [F12], so I test NS-1's three conditions. NS-1(i) is met: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:47:20 [F5][NS-1]. Conditions (ii) and (iii) both fail: at the moment of that tap the GPS placed the driver 351 m from the pickup [F5], and his closest approach all trip was 319 m — he never entered the 200 m arrival radius at all [F1]; after the tap he spent 0 s inside the radius, far short of the continuous >3 minutes the rule requires [F5][NS-1(iii)]. His post-trip statement that he "waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" is contradicted by the GPS and timeline records, which outrank statement evidence, and the chat shows the rider was in fact at the pickup point and could not find the car [F9][F12][NS-1]. Since a NS-1 condition is not fulfilled, NS-2 requires the $6.61 cancellation fee to be returned in full, and because the driver pressed "I'm Here" while GPS showed he was not at the pickup location, NS-2 also attaches flag_account [F5][F1][F6][NS-2]. The amount is the cancellation fee recorded on the fare line: $6.61, refunded as a voucher per NS-7 [F6][NS-7]. Separately, RD-6 is not triggered for the flag: the driver profile shows 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 d, so the flag rests on NS-2's abuse-of-the-waiting-button branch, not on repetition [F17][RD-6][NS-2].
